akira: quick check — we're picking the calibration corpus for the fp8/int8 sweep. do we go per-channel (one scale/zero per channel) or global per-tensor? also how aggressive on outlier clipping?

sophia: my brain says per-channel for conv/attention heads that vary a lot across channels. per-tensor is simpler but loses head-specific dynamics.

tyler: +1 per-channel for accuracy, but perf tradeoffs? per-channel increases quant math and can push us to fallback kernels in some hardware combos.

maria: correct. on A100 + cuquant, per-channel adds a ~4% perf hit in our microbench (when kernel supports it it still has overhead). but accuracy delta on some LLM layers is huge.

zeeshan: we ran a short experiment yesterday. sampling details:
```
# sample 10k sequences stratified by length & domain
python sample_calib.py --cutoffs 16,64,256 --domains web,code,chat --per-domain-prop 0.5,0.3,0.2 --seed 42 --out calib_samples.json
```
results: per-tensor avg token perplexity delta +0.8, per-channel +0.12. throughput (fp8 + quant-kernel-v2): per-tensor 14.2K tok/s, per-channel 13.6K tok/s.

akira: thanks — that matches my intuition. question: how to handle heavy-tail outliers? drop top 1%? clip to 99th percentile? keep them but label for layer-wise fallback?

sophia: we should not blindly drop outliers. they cause real behavior (KV fullness, rare tokens). propose: keep outliers but mark them and do a two-pass calibration: compute stats full corpus, then recompute scales with clipped-percentile=99.5 and keep both. use clipped for production quant params and full for regression tests.

tyler: two-pass seems reasonable. production benefits from clipped stable scales, tests detect regressions on the full distribution. implementation note: we need consistent op signatures so kernels don't allocate huge buffers for rare 2k-length tokens.

maria: on batching heuristics: if our sampler includes more long sequences we trigger different kernel selection (long-seq optimized attention kernels) which changes perf baseline. we should stratify sample to match observed seq-length histogram from prod.

zeeshan: exactly — here's a small profile snippet from the run where we accidentally over-sampled long sequences:
```
[perf] run id: 2026-03-10-1142
kernel chosen: attention_long_opt (for 30% of batches)
avg latency: 22.4ms -> (baseline 12.9ms)
kv-cache hit ratio: 0.72
fallbacks (int8->fp16): 3.4% of calls
```
we saw fallback spikes when per-channel quant triggered a less-optimized int8 path on the device.

akira: could we have the runtime prefer speed when a mixed-precision incompatibility leads to fallback? like a policy: prefer per-tensor quant when fallback rate > 1% for that layer in perf tests.

sophia: that's a neat automated rule. but we need to ensure it's explainable to the model team. maybe produce a per-layer report: "recommended quant = per-channel with expected perf hit X and expected quality win Y".

tyler: agree. also add a "safety" flag if fallback causes >2% throughput regression at tail percentiles.

maria: for sampling algorithm, suggestion: stratify by (domain, seq-length bucket, top-k token entropy). entropy helps capture rare-token heavy examples.

zeeshan: +1, and add a small held-out set with intentionally adversarial sequences (long, many uncommon tokens, repeated patterns) to catch pathological regressions. keep that set separate from calibration used to compute scales.

akira: will anyone own implementing two-pass pipeline + per-layer report? @tyler?

tyler: I can take the report generator and the fallback rule. will need maria to hook up the prod sequence histogram and zeeshan for held-out examples. ETA EOD Friday for a prototype.

sophia: I'll draft the sampling script changes (strat + entropy) and the config options for clipping percentiles.

perf-bot: scheduled job queued: calib-sweep-proto (priority: low) — will run on dev-gpu-3 when inputs ready.

akira: thanks all. final note: let's avoid naming conventions like "calib" in user-facing reports — call it "quantization tuning". keeps it clearer for PMs. :slightly_smiling_face:

zeeshan: will upload the held-out pack once sophia shares the new sampler config.

maria: filed a tiny perf issue to track kernel fallback counts per run: INF-4821.

akira: perfect. follow-ups in this thread, please paste short perf tables.
